sentences.text: On 18.03.2018 at 05.15 a.m., when the claimant/appellant was an occupant in a motor car bearing Reg.No.KL 41 D 9268 travelling through Chalakudy - Kodakara NH - 47 road from south to north direction and when the car reached near the old beverage shop at Kodakara, the driver after displaying parking signal parked the vehicle on the western side of the road.
While so, a goods carriage bearing Reg.No.KL 57 D 9287 driven by the 2nd respondent in a rash and negligent manner came from behind, hit on the car and the claimant/appellant sustained injuries.
The claimant was taken to St.James Hospital, Chalakkudy and treated as inpatient.
3. The claimant contended that he was running a light and sound shop and was a member of the Welfare Association.
In addition to that he claimed that he is a holder of a Heavy Goods Vehicle driving licence and was earning a monthly income of Rs.24,000/-.
As a result of the accident, the claimant sustained MACA NO. 1906 OF 2021 3 2024:KER:93122 severe injuries and he was referred to the Medical Board.
Ext .X1 was marked as the Certificate of the Medical Board.
In addition to that Exts.A1 to A12 were marked on the side of the claimant.
Ext. B1 - copy of the insurance policy was alone marked as the evidence on the side of the insurance company.
No oral evidence was adduced by parties.
4. The tribunal found that the claimant did not adduce any evidence to show that he was earning a monthly income of Rs.24,000/-, hence proceeded to fix the notional income at Rs.12,000/-.

In so far as the disability is concerned, the tribunal despite of noticing the fact that the Medical Board had reported that the claimant could not stand or walk without any assistance, proceeded to fix the disability at 60% and granted a total compensation of Rs.21,58,743/-.
Aggrieved by the insufficiency in the grant of compensation, the claimant has approached this Court.
5. Heard Sri.Joseph Gopuran - learned counsel for the appellant and Smt.Preethy R. Nair - learned standing counsel appearing for the insurance company.

6. The learned counsel appearing for the appellant submitted MACA NO. 1906 OF 2021 4 2024:KER:93122 that the tribunal ought to have fixed the notional income of the appellant in terms of the provisions contained under the notification issued by the State of Kerala under the Minimum Wages Act.
He further pointed out that in terms of G.O(P)No.56/2017 dated 28.04.2017, the State of Kerala has fixed the minimum wages at Rs.17,325/-.

7. In so far as fixing the functional disability is concerned, the learned counsel for the appellant relied on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Chanappa Nagappa Muchalagoda v. Divisional Manager, New India Insurance Co; Ltd. [2020 (1) SCC 796] to contend that even going by the provisions of Workmen Compensation Act 1923, the claimant-appellant is entitled to have functional disability assessed at 100%.
8.

entities.text: Chanappa Nagappa Muchalagoda v. Divisional Manager, New India Insurance Co; Ltd. [2020 (1) SCC 796]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the other hand the learned standing counsel appearing for the insurance company - Smt.Preethy R. Nair submitted that the tribunal despite the medical board's finding of disability at 45% has fixed the disability at 60% which is more than the claim of the appellant.

She further pointed out that no evidence was produced by the appellant before the tribunal to show that he was earning an MACA NO. 1906 OF 2021 5 2024:KER:93122 income of Rs.24,000/- and therefore, the Joy vs New India Assurance Company Ltd on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163796391/
2 tribunal has rightly fixed the notional income at Rs.12,000/- which does not call for the need of any interference.
9.

entities.text: Joy vs New India Assurance Company Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I have considered the rival submissions raised across the Bar.

10. In Angad Tiwari and Another vs National Insurance Co. Ltd. and Another (Civil Appeal No.10950 of 2024) decided on 01.10.2024, the Hon'ble Apex Court held that while fixing the notional income of the claimants in respect of the claim under the Motor Vehicles Act, the tribunal or the High Court could not have granted anything less that the minimum wage towards income.

entities.text: Angad Tiwari and Another vs National Insurance Co. Ltd. and Another (Civil Appeal No.10950 of 2024)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Applying the principle laid down by the apex court as above, this Court is of the considerate view that the minimum wage as fixed by the State of Kerala in G.O(P)No.56 of 2017 dated 28.04.2017 can be taken as the notional income.

Accordingly the notional income of the claimant/appellant is fixed at Rs.17,325/-.
11.

So far as the claim for enhancement of the functional disability is concerned, the claim of the appellant has to be considered in the touchstone of the principles laid down by the Apex Court in Syed Sadiq & Others v. Divisional Manager, United India MACA NO. 1906 OF 2021 6 2024:KER:93122 Insurance Company Ltd. [2014 (2) SCC 735] and also in Chanappa Nagappa Muchalagoda (Supra).

entities.text: Syed Sadiq & Others v. Divisional Manager, United India MACA NO. 1906 OF 2021 6 2024:KER:93122 Insurance Company Ltd. [2014 (2) SCC 735]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A cumulative reading of the principles laid down by the Supreme Court in the aforesaid decisions, makes it clear that a reasonable assessment has to be made with regard to the disability suffered by the claimant while deciding the question of functional disability.
A perusal of Ext.X1 which is the certificate issued by the Medical Board, specifically shows that the claimant cannot stand or walk without the assistance of a person.

The avocation of the claimant, even if it is assumed that he was running a light and sound shop or that he was a driver at the time of accident,
the nature of disability suffered by him would certainly impair his future earnings.

12. Considering the whole perspective of the facts in the present case and the facts presented before the Supreme Court in the aforementioned judgments, this Court is of the considerate view that the appellant is entitled to have the functional disability assessed at 80%.
Having fixed the functional disability at 80%, this Court is of the view that the appellant is also entitled for future prospects.
It is brought to the notice of this Court that the appellant at the time of MACA NO. 1906 OF 2021 7 2024:KER:93122 accident was aged 49 years.
Pertinently, the tribunal even though fixed the functional disability at 60%, did not grant any future prospects.
Therefore, this Court is of the view that the functional disability having been enhanced to 80%, the appellant is entitled for future prospects at 25%.
13. Coming to the further claim under the head anticipated bystander expenses, the appellant claimed an amount of Rs.5,00,000/- and only Rs.50,000/- has been granted.

In Kajal v. Jagdish Chand & Others [(2020) 4 SCC 413] the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that while granting future attendant charges or the bystander expenses as the case may be, a consolidated amount cannot be granted and it would be only proper that the multiplier system is applied.

entities.text: Kajal v. Jagdish Chand & Others [(2020) 4 SCC 413]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
14. In Jithendran v. New India Assurance Company Ltd. & another [2021 KHC Online 6653], the Hon'ble Apex Court held that in respect of a person suffering from a disability of more than 69%,
Joy vs New India Assurance Company Ltd on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163796391/
3 one attendant charges was granted.

entities.text: Jithendran v. New India Assurance Company Ltd. & another [2021 KHC Online 6653]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Joy vs New India Assurance Company Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the peculiar facts of the present case, this Court is persuaded to hold that the appellant is entitled for at least one bystander expenses or the attendant charges.

This Court is of the view that an amount of Rs.10,000/- can be fixed as the bystander expenses for one person by applying a multiplier system,
appropriate compensation could be worked out.
15.
Of course the learned standing counsel for the insurance company would point out that the interest cannot be granted on the future bystander expenses.

However, this Court is of the view that the said contention cannot be accepted in the light of the decision rendered by this Court in Master Jyothis Raj Krishna v. Sunny George [2024 KLT Online 2785].
16.

entities.text: Master Jyothis Raj Krishna v. Sunny George [2024 KLT Online 2785]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In so far as the claim for future treatment is concerned, it appears that the tribunal has not granted any compensation at all towards the said head.

Though it is to be noted that no evidence was produced before the tribunal to show that the claimant would require further treatment, it is beyond one's comprehension that a person who has suffered serious injury which has already been noticed by the Medical Board as well as by this Court, he would not incur any expenses towards future treatment.

In the absence of any specific evidence in this regard, this Court is left without any other alternative, but to grant only a consolidated amount towards the MACA NO. 1906 OF 2021 9 2024:KER:93122 future treatment.
Of course, as rightly contended by the learned standing counsel for the insurance company, the appellant is not entitled for any interest on the compensation granted under the head future treatment.
17. As an upshot of these discussions, this Court is of the considerate view that the appellant is entitled to succeed.

The enhanced compensation which the appellant is entitled is as follows:
18.
Notional income of the claimant is fixed at Rs.17,325/-, by adding 25% future prospects, the notional income will be Rs.21,656/-.
